title: This Small West Virginia Town Is Home to the Mothman—Here's How to Spend a Day There
byline: Country LivingFollowTerri RobertsonFri, October 30, 2026 at 8:40 PM UTCAdd to Preferred Sources
excerpt: Mothman lore, fall foliage, and small-town charm make Point Pleasant an ideal day trip.
content:
If you love folklore and haunted history, West Virginia is a pretty happening travel destination. There's even a statewide West Virginia Paranormal Trail with 20 stops. And one of the most popular spots that people check in on the trail is the Mothman Museum and statue on Main Street in downtown Point Pleasant.

The Mothman is tied to local tragedy—the Silver Bridge Collapse of 1967, a deadly bridge disaster. The horrific event led to new bridge safety regulations and the start of the National Bridge Inspection Program. It also solidified lore about a mysterious flying creature with red eyes.

"The first Mothman sightings were around a year before the bridge collapse," Mary Roush, a Mason County native and representative from the West Virginia Department of Tourism, explains. After the event, people viewed the Mothman as having been a warning that a major tragedy was coming to the town, she says. "It started to make people think this was more than someone just making up spooky stories to scare kids."

Eventually, the story inspired the 2002 movie The Mothman Prophecies starring Richard Gere. There's also an annual Mothman Festival the third weekend of September that draws people from all over the world to the small town—last year, it brought a record 32,000 visitors. But despite its Mothman fame, for the most part, Point Pleasant is a place that maintains its quaint small-town vibe, even though the area is growing quickly.

"Just like any other place in West Virginia, the people are down to earth, have that Appalachian hospitality, which I like to say is a little like Southern hospitality, but in our own way," Mary says.

"It is rural, but it's a nice 1-hour, or a little less, drive to Huntington and Charleston, West Virginia. I like to view Point Pleasant as a great day trip. If you're in the major hubs of West Virginia, Point Pleasant is the perfect place to go for the day to explore."

Best of all, leaf-peeping season is just gearing up here. "Mason County is in the southern part of West Virginia and is later to turn. The first week in November to the second week is usually peak for fall foliage," Mary says.

Here's what to do on a spooky small-town day adventure.

Spooky Small-Town History

Head to The World's Only Mothman Museum on Main Street for historic photos, newspaper clippings, and eyewitness accounts of the legendary creature. This popular museum also features props and rare memorabilia from The Mothman Prophecies movie, and you'll find the iconic Mothman statue by the late artist Bob Roach is right outside.

History buffs, round out your trip with a visit to the Point Pleasant River Museum, devoted to life and enterprise on the Ohio and Kanawha Rivers.

Local Shops

Point Pleasant's Main Street abounds with interesting shops. For antiques, "I love The Mason Jar," Mary says. This craft and antique mall sells a variety of primitives, antiques, and Amish-made furniture. (There's an Amish community in Leadhart, in the northern end of Mason County.) For your classic small-town mercantile situation with a little local paranormal flavor, Point Pleasant Trading Co. is the place. And for eclectic handmade gifts and other artisan-made goods, head to the Counter Point Co-op.

Tasty Eats

The Coffee Grinder is your requisite Main Street hometown coffee and lunch spot (check their Facebook for daily soup offerings). What's the Scoop is a sweet spot for hand-dipped ice cream, milkshakes, and other desserts. They even have a sundae that looks like the Mothman, cherry eyes and chocolate-bar wings. And while Village Pizza Inn is not on Main Street, it's worth a side trip. "It's a really nice little pizza place, and they actually have a Mothman Pizza." (See it here.)

Tu-Endie-Wei State Park

Tu-Endie-Wei State Park is situated right downtown and is the historical site of the Battle of Point Pleasant in 1774. Its name in the Wyandotte language means "point between two waters," referring to where the Ohio and Kanawha Rivers meet.

"That's really the heart of the town and that's also where the Silver Bridge was, connecting Point Pleasant, West Virginia, to Gallipolis, Ohio," Mary says. Today, the Silver Memorial Bridge stands in its place.

Staying a While?

While the famous Lowe Hotel is under renovation, Mary recommends scouting out a cute, historic rental, such as an Airbnb and a Vrbo.

Know a spooky small-town destination we should check out? Let us know in the comments.
